screening_decisions.reason: Not a diagnostic accuracy study; it is a mathematical model estimating required sensitivity of POC tests. No primary data, no prospective enrollment, no 2x2 data.
Not relevant: the study investigates publication bias in meta-analyses using SEER-Medicare data on bone metastases, not chlamydia POC testing.

Although it includes a prospective trial, the primary design is a decision analysis/cost-effectiveness study comparing testing strategies. It does not present standard 2x2 diagnostic accuracy data for a single index test.

Pilot diagnostic accuracy study evaluating QuickVue chlamydia rapid test against PCR in endocervical samples. Reports sensitivity, specificity, PPV. Appears to meet inclusion criteria; population likely nonpregnant women. Full-text needed to confirm prospective enrollment and exclusion of prior testing.
Clinical practice guideline, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
Commentary/discussion on rapid STI tests, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.

Prospective field evaluation of two POC tests (CRT, ACON) vs NAAT in men and women. Reports sensitivity/specificity and organism load. Meets criteria for diagnostic accuracy study in reproductive-age population.

Clinic-based evaluation of Clearview Chlamydia MF rapid test vs PCR in 1497 women at STD clinics/re-education centres. Reports sensitivity/specificity. Likely meets criteria; full-text review needed for consecutive enrollment details.
Prospective cohort study evaluating a rapid urine test for Chlamydia in 1211 men. Reports sensitivity/specificity and organism load. Meets criteria.
CDC recommendations/guidelines, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
Systematic review, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
Summary of evidence for CDC guidelines, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
Decision tree model/cost-effectiveness analysis using hypothetical cohort; no primary diagnostic accuracy data collection.

Evaluation of HandiLab-C home test vs NAAT in 231 women. Reports sensitivity/specificity. Could be considered diagnostic accuracy; however, population includes OB-GYN clinic attendees (possibly pregnant). Include conservatively; full-text should verify nonpregnant status.
Cochrane review on macrolides for chancroid; not about chlamydia POC testing.
QUADAS-2 tool description; not a primary study.
Methodological paper on bivariate meta-analysis; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
Systematic review of POC tests, not a primary study.
Individual-based modeling study on partner notification; not a diagnostic accuracy study.

Prevalence and performance study of two rapid tests (Clearview and CRT) vs PCR in Filipino women. Reports sensitivity/specificity. Appears to be a diagnostic accuracy study. Full-text should confirm nonpregnant status (OB-GYN clinic may include pregnant).
Methodological study on tests for publication bias in meta-analyses; not primary DTA study.
Review of RCTs on chlamydia screening to prevent PID; not a diagnostic accuracy study.
Cohort study on risk factors for chlamydial PID; not a diagnostic accuracy study of a rapid test.
Application of GRADE methodology; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
Review of laboratory diagnostic methods; not a primary study.
Systematic review, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
Systematic review, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
Evaluation of Biostar Chlamydia OIA assay vs culture, DFA, PCR in women attending STD clinic. Reports sensitivity/specificity. Appears to be diagnostic accuracy study.
National population-based prevalence survey; not a diagnostic accuracy study of a rapid test.

Cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study of multiple rapid tests for CT/NG/syphilis in symptomatic women; explicitly excludes pregnant women. Reports sensitivity/specificity. Meets selection criteria.

Comparison of PACE 2, amplification assays, and Clearview EIA for CT detection in 787 women from OB-GYN clinics. Reports sensitivity/specificity. Diagnostic accuracy study; however, may include pregnant women (OB-GYN setting). Include conservatively.
Evaluation of BioStar Chlamydia OIA in 261 adolescent women. Reports sensitivity/specificity. Likely meets criteria.
Pilot study evaluating Chlamydia Rapid Test Device vs PCR in 100 asymptomatic South African men. Reports sensitivity/specificity. Meets criteria.
Prevalence study using PCR only; does not evaluate a rapid/POC test against reference standard.
Review article, not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
Sentinel surveillance survey; not a diagnostic accuracy study.
Prevalence and aetiology study; does not evaluate a rapid test against a reference standard.
Clinic-based evaluation of a rapid POC test vs PCR in 278 sex workers. Reports sensitivity/specificity. Likely meets criteria.
Review article on diagnostic tests; not a primary study.
Performance evaluation study of Chlamydia Rapid Test vs PCR/SDA in 1349 women. Reports sensitivity/specificity. Meets criteria.
Study of chlamydia serovars and symptoms; not a diagnostic accuracy study of a rapid test.
Performance evaluation of CRT vs NAAT in 912 women in Suriname. Reports sensitivity/specificity. Meets criteria.
Review on immune response and infertility; not a diagnostic accuracy study.
Methodological paper on search strategies; not a primary study.
Evaluation of rapid chlamydial OIA vs LCR in 415 outpatients in Indonesia. Reports sensitivity/specificity. Diagnostic accuracy study.
Evaluation of three POC tests (Handilab-C, Biorapid, QuickVue) vs NAAT in 772 women at STI clinic. Reports sensitivity. Meets criteria.
Review of risk factors for chlamydia; not a diagnostic accuracy study.
Guidelines for laboratory diagnosis; not a primary study.

Feasibility/prototype development study with small numbers, iterative improvements, and high indeterminate results. Does not provide standard 2x2 data and is not a formal diagnostic accuracy study with consecutive enrollment.
Retrospective chart review on treatment follow-up; not a diagnostic accuracy study.
